what_its_for: Abiraterone is used to treat prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. It works by lowering the amount of male hormones (like testosterone) in your body, which can slow down or stop the growth of prostate cancer cells. It is usually used together with a steroid medicine called prednisone or methylprednisolone.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. IMPORTANT: How you take abiraterone depends on which brand you have. For Zytiga tablets: Take on an EMPTY stomach. Do not eat for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after taking this medicine. Food greatly increases the amount of drug absorbed and can cause serious side effects. For Yonsa tablets: Take WITH food (a low-fat meal). Always take abiraterone at the same time each day. Take it with your prednisone or steroid exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: The usual adult dose of Zytiga is 1,000 mg (four 250 mg tablets) taken once a day on an empty stomach. The usual adult dose of Yonsa is 500 mg (four 125 mg tablets) taken once a day with food. Prednisone (5 mg) or another steroid is taken twice a day along with abiraterone. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have liver problems. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. Then go back to your regular schedule the next day. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store abiraterone tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about safe disposal options.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat for 2 hours before or 1 hour after taking Zytiga (this does not apply to Yonsa). Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and Seville oranges, as they can affect how the medicine works in your body. Avoid alcohol or limit it, as it can worsen side effects. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should NOT touch or handle crushed or broken abiraterone tablets, as the medicine can harm an unborn baby. Men taking abiraterone should use a condom during sex with a woman who is pregnant or could become pregnant. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because abiraterone can interact with many other drugs including blood thinners, seizure medicines, and heart medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: chest pain, irregular or fast heartbeat, shortness of breath, or sudden weight gain (signs of heart problems); swelling in your legs or feet; feeling very weak or tired; dark urine, yellowing of your skin or eyes, or pain in the upper right side of your belly (signs of liver problems); severe muscle weakness; low potassium symptoms such as muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat; signs of high blood pressure like severe headache or blurred vision; signs of low cortisol (adrenal problems) such as nausea, vomiting, confusion, or dizziness; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Abiraterone does not cure prostate cancer, but it can help slow its growth and reduce symptoms. You may not feel any different right away, but blood tests (like PSA levels) and scans over time can show if the medicine is working. Some patients see improvements within a few months. Keep taking the medicine every day even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop. Do not stop taking it on your own.
special_populations: Liver problems: Abiraterone is broken down by the liver. If you have liver disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose or monitor you more closely with regular blood tests. This medicine is not recommended if you have severe liver problems. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild to moderate kidney problems, but tell your doctor if you have kidney disease. Older adults: Older adults can take this medicine, but may need to be watched more carefully for side effects like swelling and high blood pressure. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Abiraterone can harm an unborn baby and must NOT be used by women who are pregnant or breastfeeding. Male patients should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose if their partner could become pregnant.
